bull_bear.body:
- Full-line PMC supplier able to cater to diverse requirements of the paper industry from one source
- Deep manufacturing knowledge and experience across a wide range of industrial fabrics
- Long-term customer trust and credibility built on consistent performance and commitment to quality; tailored solutions, reliable delivery schedules and prompt after-sales support foster long-term relationships
- Technological expertise, strong R&D capability and need-based technical know-how from the Voith Group; R&D spend of INR 70.31 million was 3.37% of total turnover
- Positioning in sustainable papermaking — resource-efficient, performance-driven PMC products that help customers improve energy efficiency, reduce water consumption and minimise waste
- In collaboration with other Voith Group companies the Company offers holistic project packages combining product portfolio, services, digitalization, project management and consulting
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Import competition in the domestic paper industry — The Managing Director states that increasing paper imports are eroding industry competitiveness, threatening job security, discouraging investment and weakening the sector's long-term sustainability. Since the Company's PMC products are sold almost entirely to paper mills, weaker mill economics feed directly into its demand and pricing.
- Raw material and commodity price volatility — The price-risk note states that commodity price fluctuations directly or indirectly affect the price of raw materials and components used by the Company; it relies on a regular process of negotiating/adjusting prices with paper-industry customers, so recovery is not automatic. The MD adds that the Middle East conflict has contributed to inflationary pressures on key raw materials and operational inputs.
- Foreign-currency (transaction) risk across many currencies — The Company is exposed to currency risk wherever sales and purchases are denominated in a currency other than its functional currency — USD, EUR, SEK, CAD, CNY, MYR, GBP, CHF, NOK and JPY — arising from exports, group purchases and open sales/purchase orders. Policy is to hedge forex exposure through regular forward contracts to the extent possible, with residual risk evaluated case by case; sensitivity to a 1% move is disclosed for each currency.
- Geopolitical disruption to energy markets and logistics corridors — Management describes an operating environment shaped by the Middle East conflict, which has disrupted energy markets and logistics corridors, resulting in elevated input costs and supply chain constraints; the Chairman frames the environment as VUCA and references the outbreak of conflict between the USA and Iran.
- Customer credit risk concentrated in trade receivables from paper mills — Credit risk is the risk of financial loss if a customer or counterparty fails to meet contractual obligations and arises principally from receivables from customers. The Company runs a credit policy with individual creditworthiness assessment, groups customers by credit characteristics, and provides lifetime expected credit loss plus specific provisions for customers where the risk of inability to collect is high.
- Liquidity risk on financial obligations — The risk that the Company cannot meet obligations settled in cash without incurring unacceptable losses or reputational damage. Short-term liquidity is reviewed regularly by finance and the long-term position by the Board; borrowing facilities sanctioned are non-fund based limits from various bankers on an unsecured basis.
- Regulatory / labour-law change — India's new Labour Codes came into effect on 21 November 2025; the Company recognised a gratuity provision as an exceptional item after assessing their impact, showing that statutory change flows directly into cost. Management expects the reforms to improve labour efficiency and workforce management over the long term.
- Interest rate exposure concentrated in fixed-rate bank deposits — Exposure to changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Company's fixed deposits; these are fixed-rate instruments not carried at fair value through profit or loss, so a rate change at the reporting date would not affect profit or loss, but reinvestment yields on a large deposit book remain rate-dependent.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells paper machine clothing — industrial fabrics such as forming fabrics, press fabrics and dryer fabrics that are an integral part of the paper manufacturing process and that improve machine efficiency, paper quality, productivity and energy optimisation. It supplies these products primarily to paper mills, offering tailored solutions, reliable delivery schedules and after-sales support. Under Ind AS 108 the Company operates as a single segment, 'manufacturing and selling of paper machine clothing', reviewed by the CODM at an overall Company level.

outlook.body:
- Operate as a full-line PMC supplier providing customer-centric solutions from one source for an efficient and sustainable papermaking process
- Work in collaboration with other Voith Group companies to offer holistic project packages to paper manufacturers — combining product portfolio, high-end services, digitalization, project management and consulting — assuming comprehensive project responsibility and reducing complexity and interfaces for customers
- Pursue business growth in regions outside India with the support of other Voith Group companies, enabled by the Related Party Transactions proposed for shareholder approval
- Anchor strategy on the synergy between sustainability and efficiency: develop innovations with customers that enable sustainable paper production and reduce resource consumption
- Continue implementation of the 'Operational Excellence (OPEX) Programme' to improve operational efficiency and contribute to the bottom line
- Systematically invest in people with a clear focus on talent development and management, combining younger talent with senior industry mentors
- Invest in eco-friendly operations — solar photovoltaic power, rainwater harvesting — as a core pillar of corporate identity
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no new plant, line or capacity-addition project. The only capital project narrated is on the energy side: under 'Conservation of Energy' the Company reports the successful commissioning of its on-site solar photovoltaic power plant, described as a transformative milestone in its decarbonization commitment and a template for embedding sustainable technology into its infrastructure; the MD&A 'Certifications' paragraph likewise lists a rainwater-harvesting system and the installation of a solar photovoltaic power plant as eco-friendly initiatives. In the MD&A weaknesses section management notes that the high cost of technological upgradation, advanced machinery and innovation initiatives may impact operating costs and capital expenditure requirements, and the industry outlook flags a general need for capacity modernisation and efficiency improvements — but no company-specific expansion project, capacity number or commissioning timeline is disclosed. The only rupee capex quantum in this bundle is the Capital Commitments note (contracts remaining to be executed on capital account).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Company growth is directly connected to the growth of the paper industry; with rising demand from packaging, e-commerce and education, management is hopeful the Company will continue to grow
- India is the 3rd largest paper producer globally with ~6% of world paper output, and is one of the fastest growing markets, expanding at 3-4% per year driven by packaging, FMCG, e-commerce and education
- Increasing focus by paper mills on operational efficiency, reduction in downtime and enhancement of machine speeds continues to drive demand for technologically advanced PMC solutions
- Rapid expansion of e-commerce and organised retail is driving demand for containerboard, cartonboard and other packaging grades; regulatory restrictions on single-use plastics accelerate the shift to paper-based alternatives
- Specialty paper (decorative, security, filter) is one of the fastest-growing categories; rising literacy and education spend support writing and printing paper, and hygiene awareness lifts tissue/napkin consumption
- India's low per capita paper consumption versus global averages is cited as a substantial long-term expansion opportunity
- During the year the Company saw stable demand across product categories with all major product lines registering consistent growth, supported by improving conditions in the paper and packaging industry and continued customer engagement
- Consistent growth in sales and profitability was driven by heightened operational efficiencies, better utilisation of available resources and execution of business strategies, including the OPEX Programme
- Headwinds flagged: cheaper imports eroding industry competitiveness and pricing power, volatility in raw material (synthetic yarn and fibre) and energy prices, FX fluctuations, Middle East conflict disrupting energy markets and logistics corridors and raising input costs, and the long-term shift to digital platforms hurting newsprint/paper demand
- Global pulp and paper market cited at USD 351.7 billion in 2025, projected to grow from USD 357.6 billion in 2026 to USD 416.56 billion by 2035, a CAGR of 1.7%, with Asia Pacific holding a 56% share in 2025
- India's new Labour Codes effective November 2025 are expected over the long term to enhance labour efficiency, governance and workforce management practices
- The Board's Report 'Performance Overview and State of Affairs' presents an 'Orders Received' series for the five years ended 31-Mar-2026, showing orders received in FY26 above the FY25 level (chart disclosure, not reproduced here).

risks.risk: Import competition in the domestic paper industry
risks.note: The Managing Director states that increasing paper imports are eroding industry competitiveness, threatening job security, discouraging investment and weakening the sector's long-term sustainability. Since the Company's PMC products are sold almost entirely to paper mills, weaker mill economics feed directly into its demand and pricing.

risks.risk: Raw material and commodity price volatility
risks.note: The price-risk note states that commodity price fluctuations directly or indirectly affect the price of raw materials and components used by the Company; it relies on a regular process of negotiating/adjusting prices with paper-industry customers, so recovery is not automatic. The MD adds that the Middle East conflict has contributed to inflationary pressures on key raw materials and operational inputs.

The Company is exposed to currency risk wherever sales and purchases are denominated in a currency other than its functional currency — USD, EUR, SEK, CAD, CNY, MYR, GBP, CHF, NOK and JPY — arising from exports, group purchases and open sales/purchase orders. Policy is to hedge forex exposure through regular forward contracts to the extent possible, with residual risk evaluated case by case; sensitivity to a 1% move is disclosed for each currency.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to energy markets and logistics corridors
risks.note: Management describes an operating environment shaped by the Middle East conflict, which has disrupted energy markets and logistics corridors, resulting in elevated input costs and supply chain constraints; the Chairman frames the environment as VUCA and references the outbreak of conflict between the USA and Iran.

risks.risk: Customer credit risk concentrated in trade receivables from paper mills
risks.note: Credit risk is the risk of financial loss if a customer or counterparty fails to meet contractual obligations and arises principally from receivables from customers. The Company runs a credit policy with individual creditworthiness assessment, groups customers by credit characteristics, and provides lifetime expected credit loss plus specific provisions for customers where the risk of inability to collect is high.

The risk that the Company cannot meet obligations settled in cash without incurring unacceptable losses or reputational damage. Short-term liquidity is reviewed regularly by finance and the long-term position by the Board; borrowing facilities sanctioned are non-fund based limits from various bankers on an unsecured basis.

India's new Labour Codes came into effect on 21 November 2025; the Company recognised a gratuity provision as an exceptional item after assessing their impact, showing that statutory change flows directly into cost. Management expects the reforms to improve labour efficiency and workforce management over the long term.

risks.risk: Interest rate exposure concentrated in fixed-rate bank deposits
risks.note: Exposure to changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Company's fixed deposits; these are fixed-rate instruments not carried at fair value through profit or loss, so a rate change at the reporting date would not affect profit or loss, but reinvestment yields on a large deposit book remain rate-dependent.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Voith Paper Fabrics India Limited is a full-line supplier of paper machine clothing (PMC) to the Indian and export paper industry, backed by the technology and R&D of the global Voith Group.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells paper machine clothing — industrial fabrics such as forming fabrics, press fabrics and dryer fabrics that are an integral part of the paper manufacturing process and that improve machine efficiency, paper quality, productivity and energy optimisation. It supplies these products primarily to paper mills, offering tailored solutions, reliable delivery schedules and after-sales support. Under Ind AS 108 the Company operates as a single segment, 'manufacturing and selling of paper machine clothing', reviewed by the CODM at an overall Company level.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Company growth is directly connected to the growth of the paper industry; with rising demand from packaging, e-commerce and education, management is hopeful the Company will continue to grow
- India is the 3rd largest paper producer globally with ~6% of world paper output, and is one of the fastest growing markets, expanding at 3-4% per year driven by packaging, FMCG, e-commerce and education
- Increasing focus by paper mills on operational efficiency, reduction in downtime and enhancement of machine speeds continues to drive demand for technologically advanced PMC solutions
- Rapid expansion of e-commerce and organised retail is driving demand for containerboard, cartonboard and other packaging grades; regulatory restrictions on single-use plastics accelerate the shift to paper-based alternatives
- Specialty paper (decorative, security, filter) is one of the fastest-growing categories; rising literacy and education spend support writing and printing paper, and hygiene awareness lifts tissue/napkin consumption
- India's low per capita paper consumption versus global averages is cited as a substantial long-term expansion opportunity
- During the year the Company saw stable demand across product categories with all major product lines registering consistent growth, supported by improving conditions in the paper and packaging industry and continued customer engagement
- Consistent growth in sales and profitability was driven by heightened operational efficiencies, better utilisation of available resources and execution of business strategies, including the OPEX Programme
- Headwinds flagged: cheaper imports eroding industry competitiveness and pricing power, volatility in raw material (synthetic yarn and fibre) and energy prices, FX fluctuations, Middle East conflict disrupting energy markets and logistics corridors and raising input costs, and the long-term shift to digital platforms hurting newsprint/paper demand
- Global pulp and paper market cited at USD 351.7 billion in 2025, projected to grow from USD 357.6 billion in 2026 to USD 416.56 billion by 2035, a CAGR of 1.7%, with Asia Pacific holding a 56% share in 2025
- India's new Labour Codes effective November 2025 are expected over the long term to enhance labour efficiency, governance and workforce management practices
- The Board's Report 'Performance Overview and State of Affairs' presents an 'Orders Received' series for the five years ended 31-Mar-2026, showing orders received in FY26 above the FY25 level (chart disclosure, not reproduced here).

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Operate as a full-line PMC supplier providing customer-centric solutions from one source for an efficient and sustainable papermaking process
- Work in collaboration with other Voith Group companies to offer holistic project packages to paper manufacturers — combining product portfolio, high-end services, digitalization, project management and consulting — assuming comprehensive project responsibility and reducing complexity and interfaces for customers
- Pursue business growth in regions outside India with the support of other Voith Group companies, enabled by the Related Party Transactions proposed for shareholder approval
- Anchor strategy on the synergy between sustainability and efficiency: develop innovations with customers that enable sustainable paper production and reduce resource consumption
- Continue implementation of the 'Operational Excellence (OPEX) Programme' to improve operational efficiency and contribute to the bottom line
- Systematically invest in people with a clear focus on talent development and management, combining younger talent with senior industry mentors
- Invest in eco-friendly operations — solar photovoltaic power, rainwater harvesting — as a core pillar of corporate identity

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes no new plant, line or capacity-addition project. The only capital project narrated is on the energy side: under 'Conservation of Energy' the Company reports the successful commissioning of its on-site solar photovoltaic power plant, described as a transformative milestone in its decarbonization commitment and a template for embedding sustainable technology into its infrastructure; the MD&A 'Certifications' paragraph likewise lists a rainwater-harvesting system and the installation of a solar photovoltaic power plant as eco-friendly initiatives. In the MD&A weaknesses section management notes that the high cost of technological upgradation, advanced machinery and innovation initiatives may impact operating costs and capital expenditure requirements, and the industry outlook flags a general need for capacity modernisation and efficiency improvements — but no company-specific expansion project, capacity number or commissioning timeline is disclosed. The only rupee capex quantum in this bundle is the Capital Commitments note (contracts remaining to be executed on capital account).

moat.body:
- Full-line PMC supplier able to cater to diverse requirements of the paper industry from one source
- Deep manufacturing knowledge and experience across a wide range of industrial fabrics
- Long-term customer trust and credibility built on consistent performance and commitment to quality; tailored solutions, reliable delivery schedules and prompt after-sales support foster long-term relationships
- Technological expertise, strong R&D capability and need-based technical know-how from the Voith Group; R&D spend of INR 70.31 million was 3.37% of total turnover
- Positioning in sustainable papermaking — resource-efficient, performance-driven PMC products that help customers improve energy efficiency, reduce water consumption and minimise waste
- In collaboration with other Voith Group companies the Company offers holistic project packages combining product portfolio, services, digitalization, project management and consulting
